features.text: Patient is 37 years old and female.
Patient has been experiencing headaches that have been getting worse over the past few weeks.
Headaches start around the forehead and the back of the head.
Headaches are intense, rated seven out of ten when they first come on.
Headaches last throughout the day.
Tylenol helps reduce the headache intensity to four or five.
Patient has been checking blood pressure once a week for the past three weeks.
Blood pressure readings have been 160/87 and 175/92 in the past three weeks.
Patient is on lisinopril for hypertension but sometimes forgets to take it, especially on weekends.
No family history of high blood pressure or heart disease.
No dizziness, chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual changes associated with headaches.
Headaches usually start in the morning and get worse throughout the day.
Headaches do not worsen with specific activities or wake the patient up at night.
No changes in vision, speech, balance, or coordination associated with headaches.
Patient has not had any physical examinations, laboratory tests, imaging studies, or ECGs recently.
No recent changes in weight or fluid intake.
Patient only takes Tylenol for headaches and no other over-the-counter medications.
No nausea, sensitivity to light or sound, or changes in vision or mood with headaches.
Patient gets busy on weekends, which is when they tend to forget blood pressure medication.
No confusion, weakness, numbness, or seizures in the past few weeks.
No recent imaging studies like a head CT or MRI.
No recent laboratory tests such as a complete blood count, renal function tests, or endocrine evaluations.
Patient has not had a recent physical examination or imaging studies to evaluate headaches and high blood pressure.
